demos.name: Ironside Auto Works
demos.rationale: Most auto shops bury their phone number. This one puts a tap-to-call button up top and a plain list of what they fix, so a driver with a warning light knows in seconds they can call now.

demos.name: Kingsway Barber Co.
demos.rationale: A barbershop lives or dies on easy booking. This site leads with a book button and shows the cuts, prices, and hours before a visitor has to dig for them.

demos.name: Goldenrod Bakehouse
demos.rationale: People decide with their eyes here, so the site opens with the case and the day's menu, then makes it simple to find the shop or place an order.
highlights: Order or visit in a tap

demos.name: Wagtail Grooming Studio
demos.rationale: Owners want to know you'll treat their dog well. This site leads with friendly photos, the services and pricing, and a booking button that's never more than a tap away.

demos.name: TrueLine Plumbing
demos.rationale: Plumbing is urgent. The site puts the phone number and service area first, with the common jobs and trust signals right behind it.

demos.name: Lumière Nail Lounge
demos.rationale: A salon sells a feeling. Clean photos set the mood, then the services, prices, and a booking link make it easy to come in.

demos.name: Northside Coffee Co.
demos.rationale: A coffee shop needs to feel like somewhere you'd want to sit. The site leads with the space and the menu, then hours and directions for the morning rush.

demos.name: Blue Ridge Gun & Ammo
demos.rationale: A firearms shop has to look trustworthy and buttoned-up. The site stays clean and plain, with hours, location, and what's in stock easy to find.

demos.name: Lumina Aesthetics
demos.rationale: A med spa is a considered purchase. The site builds trust with calm design, clear treatments and pricing, and an easy way to book a consult.

demos.name: Pelican & Lime
demos.rationale: A restaurant site has one job: make people hungry and tell them how to order. This one leads with the food, the menu, and a clear path to order or find the place.
